## Context / Problem
Eighteen Python modules under `tests/unit` contain 32 audited prose blocks: 28 true leading docstrings and 4 full-line comment regions. Scope was revalidated against `origin/main@9e6a0e436520f67962c22dc244d7b4f77f5bee45`. Composite numeric spans around the compact sidecar block are collapsed to one real token region; executable tails are removed. The roster now calls `budget.pack_container_bins`, and a concise context-hint docstring still claims a removed orchestrator binding, so that stale block is explicitly added.

## Approach
Edit only the stable-ID blocks below. For every owned path, retain immutable before and final blobs and parse both with `ast.parse(..., type_comments=True)`. On comparison copies, remove only an allowlisted leading `Expr(Constant(str))` that is the first statement of a `Module`, `ClassDef`, `FunctionDef`, or `AsyncFunctionDef`; normalize only `ast.TypeIgnore.lineno`; require the remaining normalized ASTs to match.

Tokenize both blobs and reject every changed inline comment or non-allowlisted full-line comment. Preserve non-docstring runtime strings, regexes, prompts, imports, decorators, annotations, assertions, subprocess arguments, test data, shebangs, and complete directive-bearing physical lines exactly. Adjacent blank-line normalization is allowed only around an edited block.

## Protected false positives
All unlisted prose and every executable/directive line are protected. In particular, the current concise `D:test_roster_counted_in_prefix_estimate` text names `budget.pack_container_bins` and stays exact; the added context-hint ID alone carries the stale removed-binding claim.

## Preserved contracts and consumers
- Compaction prose keeps operation-linked portability, async delegation, test isolation, lock/stamp/log ownership, symlink canonicalization, and structural no-inline-fold evidence.
- Completion prose keeps response-denominated banking, actor-neutral durable writes, constant child scans, retry-and-loud-loss sidecars, signed diagnostics, and deterministic sampling.
- Complexity/config prose keeps shrink-only merge-base comparison, local/CI parity, fail-closed locks, warn-class tombstones, late binding, hermetic config layers, and public writer identity.
- Conflict/container/parser prose keeps JS-safe timestamps, AC-bearing cached rosters, warm abort/degrade classes, one context-hint definition with the current callable surface, and parser factories as the governing runtime grammar.
- All modules are direct pytest inputs; `tests._bank_observer` is the shared dependency for the two banking suites. Mechanism baselines and sibling workflow/mechanism tests reference the named paths. No external target-module import, `__doc__`, `inspect.getdoc`, or pydoc consumer was found.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Only declared stable-ID blocks and adjacent blank lines change; normalized-AST and token/comment comparisons pass on every owned path.
- [ ] Every edited block is shorter and retains its listed current contract while removing chronology, duplication, obvious narration, or separator ornament.
- [ ] An independent reviewer posts one leaf-linked TSV row per block: `stable_block_id<TAB>before_citation<TAB>final_citation<TAB>preserved_contract_or_consumer<TAB>directives_exact<TAB>before_words<TAB>after_words<TAB>semantic-preservation<TAB>bloat-removal<TAB>reviewer_session`.
- [ ] Before citations use `9e6a0e436520f67962c22dc244d7b4f77f5bee45:<path>#<stable-id>`; final citations use `<final-commit-sha>:<path>#<stable-id>`; every row records `directives_exact=PASS`, `semantic-preservation=PASS`, and `bloat-removal=PASS`.
- [ ] All five structured verify commands pass.

## Verification
The five DD-level commands recorded on this ticket run focused pytest (including real consumers), scoped Ruff check plus format-check, comment hygiene, owned-path `git diff --check`, and worktree-venv `make verify`. They are the executable completion oracle.
